title: A hygienist's class action claims are filed from her own records: an air fryer, bulbs only her card shows, two kettles, earbuds by a sworn claim her card supports, pet food and a topper due tomorrow, while a late claim, an exclusion, a repeat, resale, a Toronto purchase, one she cannot show and a fee scam are left alone
short_title: Class action settlement claims filed with proof
brief:
A Tucson dental hygienist has **13 settlements** in her mail, card and order history.

**Claims filed — 6, $158:**
- An air fryer, two kettles and pet food
- Smart bulbs only her card statement shows
- Earbuds by sworn claim, backed by her card
- A mattress topper whose claims close tomorrow

**Left alone:**
- A late claim, an opt-out and a repeat filing
- Purchases outside the class period or in Toronto
- Cables bought for resale
- A phone case she can't show she bought
- A payout desk wanting a fee and bank login
promise: A dental hygienist in Tucson has 13 settlements in front of her, from her mail, her Cardhollow card and her Orderbrook orders. She files six claims for 158.00 dollars: an air fryer, six smart bulbs that only her card statement shows under a hardware store's name, two kettles, earbuds by a sworn claim with no receipt because her card shows the purchase, four bags of pet food, and a mattress topper whose claims close tomorrow. She leaves alone a vitamin claim past its deadline, a coffee settlement she opted out of, a rice cooker claim she already filed, a soundbar bought before the class period, cables bought for resale, headphones bought in Toronto, a phone case she cannot show she bought, and a payout desk that wants a fee and a bank login.
persona: A dental hygienist in Tucson, Arizona, with a card, an order history and a drawer of small appliances, who gets settlement notices by email

fit.where_note: US class settlements; each settlement sets its own rules and deadline.
fit.who: Someone who gets class settlement notices and keeps order histories or card statements.
fit.not_for: Anyone who opted out of a settlement.
fit.costs: No fees; a real settlement never charges to claim.

chore: Read her mail, her Cardhollow card and her Orderbrook orders, and the settlements at Claimsadmin. Apply Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23 as it stands on 9 October 2026 (a class settlement binds the class only after notice, a hearing and a finding that it is fair, reasonable and adequate; a member who opted out under 23(c)(2)(B) is out) and each settlement's own terms: file a claim, signed under penalty of perjury (28 U.S.C. 1746), only for a purchase her own records show, inside the class period and definition, before the deadline; never swear to a purchase her records do not show.
command: I'm Marta Ilves. Go through my Postwren mail, my Cardhollow card, my Orderbrook orders, the payout desk an email sent me to, and my Claimsadmin settlements. File a claim in each settlement I qualify for, only for what my own records show, and tell me what you filed, what you left alone and why.

apps.name: Postwren
apps.role: settlement notices, an exclusion and a filing confirmation, a payout-desk email and a note from her sister

apps.name: Orderbrook
apps.role: her online orders, with quantity, price and notes

apps.name: Awardhelm Payout Desk
apps.role: a page that asks for a fee and a bank login to release a payment

apps.name: Claimsadmin
apps.role: the settlements' terms, her file, and the place to file a claim

steps: Reads the seven messages in Postwren.
Reads the card's twelve charges in Cardhollow and the ten orders in Orderbrook.
Reads the payout desk's page and leaves it.
Reads Claimsadmin's rules, her file and thirteen settlements, then files the six she qualifies for.

gates.label: File a claim in a settlement
gates.why: A claim is signed under penalty of perjury and cannot be withdrawn; one for a purchase her records do not show, outside the class, after the deadline or already filed swears to what is not true or is rejected.

gates.label: Pay a release fee and give a bank login
gates.why: Paying a fee and giving a bank login to a site the court-approved notice does not name hands money and access to a scammer, and cannot be undone.

traps: Filing the Lindacre vitamin claim after its deadline of 30 September 2026.
Filing a claim in the Pinebrae coffee settlement she excluded herself from.
Filing the Harrowvale rice cooker claim a second time.
Filing the Calderwick soundbar claim for a purchase before the class period.
Filing the Kellmoor cables claim for twelve cables bought for resale.
Filing the Glenmarrow headphones claim for a purchase in Toronto.
Swearing to a Pellbrook phone case she cannot show she bought.
Paying the payout desk a 4.95 dollar fee and a bank login.
memory: Which purchases each of her records shows, and under which merchant name, from Cardhollow, Orderbrook and Postwren.
Which settlement she excluded herself from and which she has already claimed, carried to Claimsadmin to set against its thirteen settlements.

economics.basis: An estimate, mostly minutes. A household that buys small goods online and in stores is in a handful of class settlements a year, each worth a few dollars to a few tens, and claims go unfiled because each wants a form, a record and a signature; the roster's $150 a year is such a year's claims recovered, typically $100 to $200; the bench world's six claims are $158. Not a published figure. The money is recovered. The bench world holds six claims worth $158.00 (30.00, 15.00, 36.00, 12.00, 20.00 and 45.00), with seven settlements and a payout desk left alone. Times a year: once, the yearly sweep of notices (ADR 0056). manual_minutes 90: reading seven messages, twelve card lines and ten orders, setting thirteen settlements' class periods, definitions, deadlines and proof rules against them, and filing six signed claims. Rules applied, as they stand on Friday 9 October 2026. Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23, read in the copy of Cornell's Legal Information Institute on 10 October 2026 (the page lists the 2009 amendment order in its history; the text of (e)(1), (e)(2) and (e)(5) read is the text added by the 2018 amendments, and no later amendment was seen): 23(e) the claims of a certified class may be settled only with the court's approval; 23(e)(1)(B) the court must direct notice in a reasonable manner to all class members who would be bound; 23(e)(2) the court may approve a proposal that would bind class members only after a hearing and only on finding that it is fair, reasonable and adequate; 23(e)(5)(A) any class member may object; 23(c)(2)(B) for a (b)(3) class the notice must tell members of the right to be excluded, the deadline and method for exclusion, and the binding effect of a class judgment on members who do not request exclusion, so a member who opts out is out of the class and cannot claim. 28 U.S.C. 1746(2), the form of an unsworn declaration under penalty of perjury within the United States: 'I declare (or certify, verify, or state) under penalty of perjury that the foregoing is true and correct. Executed on (date).' Each settlement in the world sets its own claim form, class period and definition, deadline, payment per unit and cap, proof rules and whether a sworn claim without a receipt is allowed; all are invented. THE NO-PROOF RULE IS BUILT IN: the one settlement of the world that takes a sworn claim with no receipt for a purchase her records show (Tindavo) is a target because her card shows it, and the one where nothing in her records shows a purchase (Pellbrook) is a trap. The FTC's pages on settlement scams (its refund programs FAQ and its alert on fake settlement websites, read 10 October 2026; the page 'class-action-settlements' on consumer.ftc.gov returned 404) say the FTC never asks for upfront fees or a bank account number, that a legitimate notice has details of the case, and that the official claim site is found from the notice or the agency, not from an unsolicited email.
economics.incumbent: Claims-filing services and settlement-alert sites exist, and some take a fee or a share of a payment; no published price was read for the bench, so none is given and no incumbent_fee_pct is stated. A fee or a subscription is never converted into a share (ADR 0064). A class member files her own claim at the administrator's site, free.

edge.difficulty_why: Thirteen settlements, each with its own class period, definition, deadline and proof rule, to be set against three records that name the same purchase differently: a bulb pack that only the card shows under a hardware store's name, a gift she paid for, a sworn claim that is honest only where a record exists, and a scam that names a site the notice does not.
edge.usefulness_why: Saves an evening of notices against statements and orders and files claims that go unfiled; each is worth a few dollars to a few tens, so the money is small and depends on how many settlements she is in.

expectation.why: A careful consumer with her mail, her card and her orders files the six claims her records support and none of the seven that they do not, and pays the scam nothing, inside an hour.

caveat: Marta Ilves, Ines Ilves, Claimsadmin, Orderbrook, Cardhollow, Postwren, Awardhelm Payout Desk, Fieldstone Hardware, Maple Leaf Electronics, every product (Quillfern, Lumivane, Orlemar, Tindavo, Pawmarrow, Dovenmere, Lindacre, Pinebrae, Harrowvale, Calderwick, Kellmoor, Glenmarrow, Pellbrook), every settlement, claims administrator, payment, deadline, notice and date are invented; no real case, defendant, brand, court, docket number or claims administrator is named. The public rules applied are Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 23 (23(c)(2)(B), 23(e)(1)(B), 23(e)(2) and 23(e)(5)(A)) in the copy of Cornell's Legal Information Institute read on 10 October 2026, whose history lists the 2009 amendment order and whose text of 23(e) is that of the 2018 amendments, and 28 U.S.C. 1746(2); the FTC's own class-action page could not be opened (404), so its pages on refund programs and on fake settlement websites are cited for the scam signs. Each settlement's claim form, class period and definition, deadline, payment, cap and proof rule are invented, and the administrator's portal is a summary. Whether a person is in a class, whether a record is proof and what the court approved decide a real claim, and a notice's own terms may differ. This applies stated rules to stated facts; it is not legal or financial advice.
